newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KEDO opens laison office at N.Korean reactor site.
newsitem.headline: KEDO opens laison office at N.Korean reactor site.

text.p: A consortium of nations building two nuclear reactors in North Korea said it opened a liaison office at the plant's construction site on Monday, South Korean newspapers reported.

The Korea Herald said staff members of the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) at the new office in the northeastern city of Shinpo were Lee Hyon-joo and Seo Hoon of South Korea's Foreign Ministry, John Hogg and Dennis Droney from the U.S. State Department and Takane Kazumasa from the Japanese Foreign Ministry.
The reports appeared in the Tuesday editions of the newspapers, which are usually made available the night before their printed publication date.
KEDO, which includes the United States, South Korea and Japan, was formed in 1995 to finance the building of two light-water reactors according to a 1994 agreement between Pyongyang and Washington.
The agreement, signed in Geneva, was designed to halt North Korea's suspected nuclear weapons programme.
Ground-breaking for site preparation was scheduled for next month, a South Korean KEDO official said earlier on Monday.
The opening of the liaison office comes amid long-running efforts to bring peace to the Korean peninsula.
Senior officials from the two Koreas, the United States and China are due to meet in New York on August 5 to pave the way for talks aimed at hammering out a permanent peace settlement.
North and South Korea remain technically at war as their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not a peace treaty.
Separately, 9,000 tonnes of construction equipment, originally scheduled to be shipped to Shinpo last Friday, left for the North on Monday after being delayed due to a typhoon.
